dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: Even though my new life here is not easy, by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, I'm still filled with hope.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: New life?

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: I used to be a snake handler in the rain forest. I recently moved to the harbor and make my living as a busker.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: I thought life at the port would be more convenient than wandering in the wild. Only after coming here did I find out that it's not easy for the locals here, too.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: In the rain forest, we were awakened by Dusk Birds early in the morning and searched for food. At the port, people get up to work alongside the sound of trumpets of the fleet.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: I'll never return to the simple life in the rainforest, but I shall always remember the time spent singing stories under the moon with my companions.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: Colorful mushrooms and fruits roasting on the fire. A rainbow-like tapestry before our eyes... Ah, good times.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Greater Lord Rukkhadevata...

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: Isn't the story of the Greater Lord the best proof of hope?

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: She sacrificed herself to defend the land of Sumeru from calamity.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: She may have passed away, but other lives continue to thrive on the land and in the sea.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: Ah... The songs that had been sung among Vanara are popping into my mind again.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: I should replay them next time. I'm sure to make more money with that. After all, who in Sumeru doesn't love the Greater Lord?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: See you. Things will get better still!

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: My new life here is not easy, but thanks be to the Dendro Archon — I'm still filled with hope.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me more about the Dendro Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: Ah, and isn't the story of the Greater Lord the best evidence for hope?

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: She sacrificed her power to defend the land of Sumeru from calamity.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: She did this so that other life, whether on land or sea, might continue to thrive.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: Ah... The songs that had been sung among Vanara are popping into my mind again.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: I should perform them again next time — that'll fetch me a good sum of Mora for sure. After all, who in Sumeru doesn't love the Dendro Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Forest Watchers might have a problem with that.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: Th—They can't know it, for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: I bumped into a long-tailed Forest Watcher once and got my noggin beaten. It really hurt!

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: But if you think about it, it's actually quite some memory, to be dragged by rescue dogs all the way to Gandharva Ville. You should try it sometime.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: Just kidding! It's important to listen to the Forest Watchers for your own safety.

dialogues.speaker: Gulabgir
dialogues.text: After all, the rainforest is full of both safe ingredients that can make a delicious meal and inedible stuff one should avoid.
